blocks.text: FloppyData in 2026: what you get

FloppyData sells proxies the way prepaid phone plans sell minutes: one flat $1/GB balance that works across residential, mobile and datacenter pools. Static residential IPs start at $1.79 each in monthly bundles (20 for $49) with unlimited bandwidth. It is one of the cheapest ways into residential traffic, but it is a newer brand with less independent benchmarking than the established names.

Strengths: Flat $1/GB on any volume; One balance across residential, mobile and datacenter; Cheap static residential bundles with unlimited bandwidth; Free cloud anti-detect browser. Weak spots: Newer brand with limited independent testing; Pool-size claims disputed by some reviewers; Mixed customer-support reviews.
Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

Proxys.io is a per-IP proxy shop rather than a bandwidth network. Its catalog covers shared IPv4 (up to three users per IP), dedicated IPv4, cheap IPv6 from $0.13 per address, premium residential IPv4, rotating residential packages and SIM-based mobile proxies. You rent each IP for days or months, bandwidth is generally unlimited on dedicated IPs, and a 24-hour refund window replaces a trial. It is popular with affiliate marketers and multi-account operators who want fixed addresses rather than a rotating pool.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
Pricing: FloppyData vs Proxys.io

FloppyData charges a flat $1/GB for rotating traffic, and the same balance works for residential, mobile and datacenter IPs. Static residential proxies are sold in monthly bundles from $1.79 per IP (20 IPs for $49), and static datacenter IPs from $0.79 per IP.

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; FloppyData comes to about $10. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; FloppyData comes to about $100. Both FloppyData and Proxys.io work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

FloppyData and Proxys.io do not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. FloppyData lists '65M+ claimed (disputed)' and Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, FloppyData lists 148 (residential) countries and Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage. On targeting, FloppyData offers country and city, while Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, FloppyData offers rotating or sticky sessions, and Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?
General web scraping: FloppyData. FloppyData has the edge here. Why: cheap, but with limited independent benchmarking. How Proxys.io compares: it is a per-IP shop, not a large rotating pool.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. FloppyData: workable for light tasks. Proxys.io: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: Proxys.io wins. The deciding factor for Proxys.io: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. The limitation on the FloppyData side: cheap static residential IPs and a free anti-detect browser.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: FloppyData. FloppyData has the edge here. Why: city targeting at a flat rate. How Proxys.io compares: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.

Ad verification and geo-testing: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With FloppyData: limited targeting depth and published data. With Proxys.io: limited geo depth. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Tight budgets: FloppyData wins. The deciding factor for FloppyData: a flat $1/GB on any volume. The limitation on the Proxys.io side: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. FloppyData: No free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. Verification and payment rules differ too. FloppyData: Light. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test FloppyData and Proxys.io before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle FloppyData vs Proxys.io faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (FloppyData: no free trial; free browser extension for testing a few locations; Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, FloppyData comes out ahead in 3, Proxys.io in 1, and 2 are ties. That makes FloppyData the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: FloppyData is strongest for small budgets and experiments, while Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
